investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but have exhausted their allocatable quota; the other four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also ruled out because no lower-priority victims exist on the two eligible nodes. As a result, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs never received a running VM, the probe timed out after ~124–145 s, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create received zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing).

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — all allocatable VM slots are occupied by existing pods, leaving no room for new remote-agent pods.

[Likely secondary] Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, so the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of their general capacity.
[Possible] A burst of concurrent remote-agent creation requests (e.g., from multiple eval runs or user traffic) exhausted the VM quota before this probe's pod was submitted.

[Possible] One or both kata-capable nodes degraded (e.g., kubelet not ready, node cordoned, or kata-agent process unhealthy) reducing effective VM capacity to zero without the node being fully removed from the cluster.
[Lower likelihood] The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit per node was recently reduced via a node configuration or device-plugin change, shrinking total cluster capacity below the concurrent demand.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but have exhausted their allocatable quota; the other four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also ruled out because no lower-priority victims exist on the two eligible nodes. As a result, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs never received a running VM, the probe timed out after ~124–145 s, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create received zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing).

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — all allocatable VM slots are occupied by existing pods, leaving no room for new remote-agent pods.

[Likely secondary] Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, so the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of their general capacity.
[Possible] A burst of concurrent remote-agent creation requests (e.g., from multiple eval runs or user traffic) exhausted the VM quota before this probe's pod was submitted.

[Possible] One or both kata-capable nodes degraded (e.g., kubelet not ready, node cordoned, or kata-agent process unhealthy) reducing effective VM capacity to zero without the node being fully removed from the cluster.
[Lower likelihood] The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit per node was recently reduced via a node configuration or device-plugin change, shrinking total cluster capacity below the concurrent demand.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-30 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: 0/6 nodes were available due to insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on 2 eligible nodes and node affinity/selector mismatches on the remaining 4. Because the remote agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or receiving a runtime response, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) empty and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector requirements. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints and are therefore ineligible regardless of resource availability. Preemption cannot resolve the situation because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted by the eval runner is stuck in Unschedulable state for the full timeout window (~124–150 s), and no agent is ever created, making it impossible for the runtime check to produce any evidence output.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: the cluster has consumed all available peer-pod VM slots, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or insufficient eligible node count: only 2 of 6 nodes match the pod's affinity/selector, creating a very small scheduling domain. If those 2 nodes are at capacity, there is no fallback. A misconfigured affinity rule could be artificially restricting the eligible pool.

Tertiary — peer-pod VM quota set too low for concurrent eval workloads: if multiple eval runs or production workloads compete for the same kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, the quota may be undersized for the observed concurrency.

Lower confidence — a stuck or leaked remote agent pod from a prior eval run consuming a VM slot and not being cleaned up: the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (source-context line 1916) is intended to release resources, but a prior crash or timeout could leave a pod occupying a slot.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm resource usage on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes to determine whether slots are fully consumed by production workloads, stuck eval pods, or both.
Check for leaked remote agent pods from prior eval runs that may not have been cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916). Terminate any orphaned pods to free VM slots.

Review the node affinity/selector rules on the remote agent pod template to determine whether the restriction to 2 of 6 nodes is intentional. If not, expanding the eligible node pool would increase scheduling resilience.
Assess whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on the 2 eligible nodes is sized appropriately for the combined load of production remote agents and eval probe pods running concurrently.

Consider adding a pre-flight check in the eval runner that queries available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity before attempting agent creation, so the check can emit a more actionable SKIP or WARN status instead of timing out after 120–150 s.

Monitor whether the feature's outage threshold has been crossed: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are both required checks (features.json lines 183–184) and both failed, satisfying the outageAfterFailures=2 condition for the remote-agents feature (features.json line 188).

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity remaining on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a misconfigured pod spec or quota enforcement bug.
If the remote-agent-create sibling check passed in a concurrent or immediately subsequent run while VM capacity was unchanged, the failure would not be attributable to cluster-wide exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the root cause would be localized to the runtime check's specific pod configuration rather than shared VM capacity.

If the scheduler message changed to a different error (e.g., image pull failure, OOMKilled, or a different resource constraint) on re-run, the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion diagnosis would need revision.
If no pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots when the cluster is inspected, the quota may be set to zero or the resource may be misconfigured rather than exhausted by running workloads.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity across all cluster nodes and warns when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), before pod scheduling is attempted.

Add a node-affinity-coverage check that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum (e.g., at least 3), alerting when the eligible pool shrinks to a level where a single capacity event causes total scheduling failure.

Add a remote-agent-cleanup check that detects orphaned remote agent pods (Pending or Running beyond a TTL) and fails if any are found, catching resource leaks from prior eval runs before they exhaust VM quota.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to emit a structured evidence field indicating the scheduling outcome (scheduled vs. unschedulable) so future failures can be distinguished between scheduling failures and post-scheduling runtime failures without reading raw scheduler messages.
